about.title: Garden Grove Slip & Fall and Premises Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Garden Grove is a busy retail town. Grocery stores, strip malls and restaurants line Garden Grove Boulevard, Brookhurst Street and Chapman Avenue, and roughly 175,000 residents move through them every week alongside visitors coming off SR-22. When a trip goes wrong because of a wet produce aisle, a parking lot pothole or a broken stair rail at an apartment complex, California premises liability law asks a specific question: did the property owner know about the hazard, or should they have known, and did they fail to fix it or warn you? That "notice" element is where these cases are decided, so the sooner someone starts gathering photos, incident reports and store video, the stronger your position. You generally have two years to file, but far less time if the property belongs to the City of Garden Grove, Orange County or another public agency. LawProactive is not a law firm. We are a free service that connects you with an independent Orange County attorney who takes premises cases on contingency, meaning no fee unless there is a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why Garden Grove Residents Use LawProactive

items.title: Notice Is the Whole Case
items.desc: California requires proof that the owner knew or should have known about the hazard. The attorneys in our network know how to look for inspection logs, prior complaints and cleaning schedules that show what the property actually knew.

items.title: Video Disappears Fast
items.desc: Most Garden Grove shopping centers keep surveillance footage for only days or weeks before it is overwritten. Getting a preservation demand out early can be the difference between a clear record and a memory contest.

items.title: Deadlines Vary by Owner
items.desc: You typically have two years to file against a private business, but a claim involving city, county or state property runs on a much shorter clock. An attorney can sort out who owns the site before that window closes.

items.question: I fell on a cracked sidewalk in Garden Grove. Is the city responsible?
items.answer: It depends on who owns and maintains that stretch of sidewalk, which can be the City of Garden Grove, Orange County, Caltrans near SR-22, or the adjacent property owner. Claims against a public entity follow a much shorter deadline than the standard two years, and missing it can end the case before it starts. Photograph the exact spot and its location right away so an attorney can determine ownership quickly.

items.question: The store says I wasn't watching where I was going. Does that end my claim?
items.answer: No. California uses pure comparative fault, so if you are found partly responsible, your recovery is reduced by that percentage rather than eliminated. The owner still has to answer for whether they knew or should have known about the hazard and what they did about it.

items.question: What should I do in the first few days after a fall?
items.answer: Get medical care and keep every record. Write down the date, time and precise location, take photos of the hazard and your footwear, and ask the business for a copy of any incident report. Then request in writing that they preserve surveillance video, since footage is often erased within a short period. LawProactive can connect you with an attorney who will send that request on your behalf at no cost to you.
